stem: A nurse counts the resting respiratory rate of a calm healthy newborn. Which range is expected?
rationale: NCBI Bookshelf Nursing Health Promotion (2025), Table 14.5c, lists the normal respiratory-rate range for a newborn to one month as 30–60 breaths per minute. Therefore B is correct. The other ranges fall below or above the cited expected newborn range.
educational_objective: Identify the expected resting respiratory-rate range of a healthy newborn as 30–60 breaths per minute.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf (Open RN)
source_document_title: Nursing Health Promotion — Table 14.5c Respiratory Rate by Age
source_locator: Table 14.5c, Respiratory Rate by Age: Newborn to one month — 30–60 breaths per minute.
source_claim_supported: Normal respiratory rate for newborn to one month is 30–60 breaths/min.
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — expected growth/development principles and health assessment.
correction_summary: Standardized capitalization/formatting across all options; clinical content and key remain unchanged.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — the cited NCBI table gives exactly 30–60 breaths/min for newborn to one month.
